skills.content:
---
name: security-audit-bot
description: >-
  Use when the owner asks to audit a repository, check whether their code is
  safe, wants a security review, or asks what to rotate after a hosting platform
  incident such as Railway's.
---
The full runbook is in the bot's repo, https://github.com/PhillipHolland/security-audit-bot (tag v0.3.0). If `$HOME/security-audit-bot` does not exist, or is not on v0.3.0 (`git -C $HOME/security-audit-bot describe --tags`), move any old copy aside and run `git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.3.0 https://github.com/PhillipHolland/security-audit-bot $HOME/security-audit-bot`. Then Read `$HOME/security-audit-bot/skills/security-audit-bot/SKILL.md` and follow it exactly. "This bot's repo root" is `$HOME/security-audit-bot`, so run every `python3 scripts/sab.py ...` command with that as the working directory. If the clone fails, tell the owner and stop.

Short version: authorization gate first (the owner must say it's their code, `sab.py check-authorization`), then a read-only shallow clone of the target, then `sab.py preflight` (scanner leads plus checks for AI-built apps and PHP, deduped, compared with the previous run, accepted findings hidden via `sab.py accept`). Then quick triage, or, after quoting the size and cost from preflight and getting the owner's yes, Cloudflare's six-phase security-audit skill (a pinned clone made by `sab.py setup`). For Railway users, `sab.py platform-check <repo> --platform railway` gives a key rotation checklist built from the repo only. Every report opens with "What to do first". Run `sab.py report-lint` before sending. Give a `sab.py share-line` only when the owner asks. Findings stay private to the owner.
